title: CoRAL: Collaborative Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models Improve Long-tail Recommendation

problem.claim: Long-tail recommendation is challenging because traditional recommender systems face data sparsity and data imbalance.

gap.claim: LLM-based recommendation systems often rely only on item semantic meaning and neglect collaborative user-item interaction information, which can misalign reasoning with task-specific collaborative information.

contributions.claim: A collaborative retrieval-augmented LLM approach, CoRAL, incorporates collaborative evidence directly into prompts.
CoRAL identifies an optimal interaction set through sequential decision-making and a reinforcement-learning-based retrieval policy.
The approach uses retrieved user-item interactions to analyze shared and distinct user preferences and summarize item-attraction patterns.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that CoRAL significantly improves LLM reasoning abilities on specific recommendation tasks.
The authors report that CoRAL more efficiently explores collaborative information through reinforcement learning.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-tail recommendation is difficult because of sparsity and imbalance.
LLMs may infer user preferences from few interactions, but existing LLM-based systems neglect collaborative interaction information.
CoRAL retrieves collaborative evidence, incorporates it into prompts, and uses it to align reasoning with interaction patterns.
Because prompt capacity is limited, CoRAL selects minimally sufficient interactions using sequential decision-making and reinforcement learning.
The authors report improved reasoning and more efficient exploration of collaborative information.

source_observation.claim: Neglecting collaborative user-item interaction information can misalign LLM reasoning with task-specific dataset information.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation systems using LLMs may benefit from combining semantic item information with interaction-derived evidence.

application.claim: For sparse recommendation settings, retrieve relevant collaborative interactions and include them as reasoning evidence.

exception.claim: Prompt capacity limits may make indiscriminate inclusion of collaborative information ineffective; interaction selection is needed.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated recommendation tasks, datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the reinforcement-learning algorithm, retrieval policy details, or selected interaction-set size.
